subject: ScaleProof discovery — SLOs, priming strategy and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@edgecloud.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: ScaleProof discovery — SLOs, priming strategy and next steps

Hi Elena / EdgeCloud team,

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation and I wanted to capture the concrete SLO/operational items we discussed so we have a shared checklist. I kept the notation tight so we can hand this to ops/bench quickly. Attachment: scaleproof_slo_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet) and mutual_action_plan.md (markdown).

Summary (post-call):
- Primary workload: streaming chat assistant (long-form responses, average 160 tokens per response).
- Latency targets: p50 first-token <= 150ms across our hosted route; p95 end-to-end response <= 900ms for short responses (~80 tokens). Tail behavior requirements: p99 < 2.5s for production traffic.
- Concurrency & throughput: expected steady-state 120 concurrent streaming connections; burst to 480 concurrent for 3–7 minutes during peak events.
- Scale-up window: desire < 120s to deliver new capacity into the warm pool path; preferred warm-pool handoff time <= 45s once warm instances are online.
- Warm pools: target 6–10 prewarmed instances per region (we recommended starting at 8 and iterating).
- Queueing/fallthrough: short queueing is acceptable (< 3s per request) but must not drop active streaming sessions; fallback model variant allowed for graceful degradation.
- Observability: token-level traces, per-request route tags, and a per-commit SLO readout (p50/p95/p99) required.

Action items we committed to:
1) Redwood: run a customer-specific benchmark using EdgeCloud prompt set (we'll request a sample set of 50 prompts).
2) EdgeCloud: share production traffic shape (5-minute and 1-hour histograms) and a redacted sample of slow traces.
3) Redwood: provide configuration baseline (warm-pool size, priming sequence, batch sizing) and an expected cost delta for 8 vs 12 prewarmed nodes.
4) Schedule: hands-on demo to validate warm-pool lifecycle and streaming tail behavior — proposed dates below.

Proposed demo windows: Aug 4–6 (PST) or Aug 11–13 (PST) — pick 2 options and we'll lock.

Please confirm the traffic sample and procurement timeline so we can prioritize the benchmark run.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with infra: 

- Traffic shape: we'll export 5-minute and 1-hour histograms for the week of June 14–20 and share them by EOD Tuesday (attached as ops_hist_export.json).
- Prompts: Tom will curate a 50-prompt set (mix of short/long responses) and share it privately.
- Burst expectations: the 480 concurrent number is realistic but typically only lasts 2–4 minutes; occasionally it stretches to ~8 minutes during releases.
- Warm pools: our procurement policy wants to minimize idle reserved capacity. Can Redwood offer an autoscaling path that stays within the p95 latency target while keeping the warm pool < 10 nodes? If not, we may need to discuss a reserved-commitment model.
- SLA language: please provide the draft SLA/credit language that corresponds to the p99 <= 2.5s requirement so procurement can review.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) What sampling/bench tooling will you run against our prompts? Are you able to simulate our actual release spike shape?
2) If warm-pool handoff is >45s, what are the default queueing behaviors (max wait, prioritization)?

Tom (cc'd) — can you attach the release-day traffic dump and confirm the longest sustained burst you observed in Q2?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Director, Platform Engineering
EdgeCloud

Ben / Sean — forwarding the thread from EdgeCloud. Quick internal notes on pricing/commit options before we reply: attachment: pricing_tiers.pdf.

Pricing options (high level):
- On-demand: no commit, slightly higher per-hour cost for prewarmed instances. Good for proof-of-concept; not ideal for sustained bursts.
- Committed reserved blocks: 6/12/24-month blocks that materially lower unit costs and let us recommend a larger warm pool with reserved capacity. EdgeCloud will need procurement language for any p99 SLA credits.
- Hybrid: reserved minimum (e.g., 4 nodes) + dynamic warm pool to hit transient bursts. This is often a good compromise for customers that want to limit reservation while hitting p95/p99 targets.

Technical notes to include in our reply to EdgeCloud: we should propose an initial benchmark that explicitly measures: cold-start time for a fresh instance, warm-pool handoff latency, p95/p99 token tail under the release spike shape, and queueing behavior with prioritized streaming sessions. Recommend we offer two benchmark runs: one on our hosted cluster (fast validation) and another using EdgeCloud traffic replay (most realistic).

I'll draft the SLA language and a short summary of the expected cost delta for 8 vs 12 prewarmed nodes. Ben — can you confirm the demo windows you proposed (Aug 4–6 or Aug 11–13)? I'll prepare the pricing appendix for procurement once we pick a date.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
